title: A visitor at the open door while Lucy holds her bed
step: Program cover — the whole picture of what the program is for
note: Written after the fact, on 2026-09-04. This is one of the six pictures drawn by hand through a chat window before the pipeline existed, so it never had a spec; this one reconstructs the shipped picture so that it can be redrawn under cool-flat-v2 with everything but the room unchanged.  Round 127 (v2) held every content clause and put the tallest head at 15% of the height, which the 21:9 hero band clips at the forehead. The framing is now stated as an override with the band's own numbers. Round 128 (v2) drew the figures larger still (tallest head at 5%). The v1 source is now attached as continuity:room — its distance passed the 21:9 band — and the text names the picture as a wide shot with small figures.
scene: Interior entry hall, side view, camera at standing eye level, the widest view of the room in the set: a clear span of oak floor from the left of the frame to the front door on the right. Three figures, and all three must read at 84 pixels. On the left the handler stands facing right, relaxed, holding a black leash that hangs in a deep slack curve to Lucy. In the middle Lucy sits square and upright on her grey dog bed, a few feet inside the hall, facing the door with her head up and her ears attentive, calm rather than excited, all four feet on the bed. On the right the front door stands wide open, swung into the room, and the guest stands on the porch in the doorway — not inside — with his hands relaxed at his sides, black cap, glasses, blue hoodie over a white tee, dark trousers; pale daylight and flat spruce foliage behind him. The doormat lies inside the threshold. Nothing else in the room. THIS IS A COVER, cut to a centred square for the library and to a wide 21:9 band for the program hero, so group the three tightly: everything essential inside the middle 75% of the width, all three heads in the middle band of the height, the top of the tallest head about a quarter of the way down the frame, and clear wall above every head. THE GUEST AND ROOM ATTACHMENTS WERE DRAWN IN THE OLD LAVENDER ROOM: take his face, glasses, black cap and blue hoodie from it and nothing else. The wall colour comes from the style block — warm off-white plaster — and nothing in that attachment overrides it. Every person has exactly two arms and two hands, each hand on its own sleeve; the treat pouch at the handler's right hip hides no spare hand. Lucy wears the purple collar with the round blue tag and no harness. FRAMING, AND THIS PARAGRAPH WINS OVER ANYTHING ABOVE: the app cuts a 21:9 band out of this picture that keeps only the middle 57% of the height — from about 21% down to about 79% — so EVERY HEAD MUST SIT BELOW ONE QUARTER OF THE HEIGHT AND EVERY FOOT ABOVE THREE QUARTERS. Put the top of the tallest head at 25% of the height, not higher: there is a clear band of empty wall above every head equal to a quarter of the picture. The three figures fill the middle half of the height, and the three of them together sit inside the middle 70% of the width. If a head touches the top quarter of the picture, the picture is wrong. THIS IS A WIDE SHOT AND THE FIGURES ARE SMALL: match the attached room picture for the camera distance exactly — each standing figure is only about half the height of the picture, with a band of empty wall above every head as deep as a standing figure is from the waist up, and empty floor below. The picture is mostly wall and floor; the people and the dog are small in it. Do not draw them larger than the attachment does. Two rounds have come back with the heads at the top edge because the figures were drawn too large.
mustBeTrue: all three figures are complete and inside the middle 75% of the width with every head in the middle band of the height and a clear band of wall above the tallest, so neither the centred square nor the 21:9 band clips a head; the leash runs from the clip on Lucy's collar to the handler's hand in a slack curve; Lucy sits on the bed with all four feet on it, facing the door and not up at the handler; the guest stands on the porch side of the open door and not inside the room, in his black cap, glasses and blue hoodie; and the door's four-pane window is visible in the open leaf.
